display.purpose: The name only, inside the wide hero axes, sized to the panel with container units.

lede.purpose: The single research statement under the hero, 34ch.

title.purpose: Entry headings and the Updates heading.

body.purpose: All reading text at a 68ch measure, old-style proportional figures.

caption.purpose: Figure captions, profile links, slider row; DejaVu Sans.

tick.purpose: Axis tick values in label gray.

motion.name: ease-state

narrative.overview:
The page is laid out the way a machine-learning paper presents results: a white figure ground, imshow panels framed by thin black spines with outward ticks, numbered figure captions, and bracketed [n] citations that jump to a reference list. Every visual device is borrowed from matplotlib and the publication page, never from web-template furniture. The only material is grayscale Gaussian noise, i.i.d. standard-normal samples painted one per pixel on a canvas and scaled up with crisp, pixelated edges.

Two voices carry the type: STIX Two Text, a scientific serif, for the name, headings and reading text; DejaVu Sans, matplotlib's default label face, for everything a plot would label (ticks, captions, dates, navigation, buttons, reference numbers). Color is almost absent. The matplotlib default cycle supplies the only two hues: tab:blue for links and focus, tab:orange for the one live marker. Density is generous and editorial: long section gaps, a 68ch measure, and no containers around content.

Motion is one authored moment. On load the hero samples from t = 1 to t = 0, the name and portrait resolving out of noise, and the t slider lets the visitor re-noise both panels. Nothing else on the page animates in.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, near-black ink, three gray steps for text hierarchy.
1px black spines with 5px outward ticks frame every image and the time axis of dated entries.
Pixelated N(0,1) grayscale noise as the single material.
tab:blue links; tab:orange on the slider handle only.
Square corners everywhere; no shadows, gradients or cards.
Serif for reading, DejaVu Sans for anything a plot would label.

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: Tab orange appears on exactly one element: the handle of the live t slider. Bullets, highlights and badges stay in ink or tab blue.

rules.name: The Matplotlib Cycle Rule
rules.body: New hues come from the matplotlib default cycle in its order, and only for a plotted or interactive mark. Nothing is decorated with color.

rules.name: The Plot Label Rule
rules.body: If matplotlib would draw it as a label (ticks, axis titles, captions, dates, numbers in brackets, controls), it is DejaVu Sans with tabular lining figures. Everything a reader reads as prose is STIX.

rules.name: The Math Italic Rule
rules.body: Variables in captions and axis titles (t, x, ε, N) are STIX italic at about 1.12 to 1.15em, even inside DejaVu text.

rules.name: The Figure Is Flat Rule
rules.body: A surface that needs separation gets a 1px spine or hairline, never a shadow or a tinted card.

dos: Do frame every image or figure as axes: 1px ink spine, 5px outward ticks, DejaVu tick labels, and a "Figure n." caption.
Do use the noise field, with real N(0,1) samples at the panel's own pixel grid, as the placeholder for missing imagery.
Do cite claims with bracketed [n] numbers that link to the reference list.
Do keep tab orange on the slider handle alone, and links in tab blue (#1f77b4).
Do keep every corner square (0px) and every rule 1px.
Do give any new motion a reduced-motion state that shows the settled result.
donts: Don't add cards, tinted panels, shadows, gradients or rounded tiles; separation is a spine or a hairline.
Don't use tab orange for text, bullets or highlights.
Don't set prose in DejaVu or labels in STIX; the split follows the Plot Label Rule.
Don't add entrance animations beyond the hero sampling run.
Don't use colored or smoothed noise; it is grayscale and pixelated.

motion.name: develop
motion.purpose: Print develops from blank paper; starts 450ms after load at 45% visibility; timer counts to 1:30.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Print settles into the liquid while developing.

motion.name: ripple
motion.value: SVG feTurbulence fractalNoise 0.006 0.018 ↔ 0.009 0.024 (2.8s loop) → feDisplacementMap scale 22,12,5,0 at 0/.4/.75/1; overscan scale 1.065,1.036,1.016,none inside overflow:hidden
motion.purpose: Developer ripples on fine pointers; the photo edge stays square.

motion.name: fly-to-line
motion.value: 1150ms cubic-bezier(.45,0,.2,1); peel -14px at .14, arc -9deg at .55, overshoot +6px 7deg at .88
motion.purpose: Developed print flies to its pin.

motion.name: swing
motion.value: 1.9s cubic-bezier(.3,.6,.3,1); rotate 16,-10,6,-3,1.2,0deg; clip snap scaleY 1.25 over 350ms
motion.purpose: Print swings on its clothespin after landing.

motion.name: flicker
motion.value: 560ms linear opacity steps of a #f3f5f1 overlay, ending .82
motion.purpose: Fluorescent tubes catching when the lights go on.

motion.name: lights-view-transition
motion.value: groups .8s cubic-bezier(.22,.8,.24,1); root .55s; stagger 45ms per print, capped 540ms
motion.purpose: Prints move from trays to the wall.

motion.name: loupe-lift
motion.value: 820ms cubic-bezier(.2,.75,.25,1); from source rect → translateY(-1.4rem) scale(1.035) rotateX(7deg) at .62 → none; perspective 1400px
motion.purpose: Print lifted toward the viewer; info and controls rise .55s after .3s; close 200ms fade.

motion.name: loupe-step
motion.purpose: Previous and next in the loupe.

motion.name: print-hover
motion.purpose: Developed print lifts slightly on hover.

extensions.reducedMotion: Every print loads developed and every pin hung; no develop, ripple, fly or swing. Lights switch instantly with no flicker or view transition. Loupe opens, steps and closes without animation. Hover nudges, print and sign transitions and smooth scrolling are off. Turning the preference on mid-visit settles everything. If the script fails within 4s, all prints show.

narrative.overview:
The gallery is a working darkroom lit by one safelight. Each photograph is a sheet of paper in a developer tray; it develops as the visitor reaches it (blank paper, then shadows, then full tones, while the developer ripples), then flies up to a sagging drying line and swings on a wooden clothespin. A lit IN USE sign is the light switch: the room flickers to white fluorescent light and every print is laid out on wires across a grey wall, with the empty tubs on the bench below. Any print can be lifted out to look at closely.

Two voices carry the type: Barlow Condensed for darkroom signage, timers and labels; Permanent Marker for grease pencil on masking tape. Text is sparse; the photographs lead. Photographs always keep their true colours and their own aspect ratios once developed.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black red room with a single safelight pool; a neutral grey room with the lights on.
Bright photo-paper prints with white borders, sized from the image's own aspect ratio.
Physical materials: tray rim and liquid, masking tape, wire and clothespins, a sign plate, bench tubs.
Condensed uppercase signage plus grease-pencil handwriting.
One motion story per print: develop, fly, hang, swing. Every state appears instantly under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Two Lights Rule
rules.body: The room has exactly two states, safelight and lights on, and every surface colour is a token that both states redefine. A new surface takes its colour from these tokens, never from a third palette.

rules.name: The Untouched Print Rule
rules.body: Nothing tints a developed photograph: the safelight colours the room, the rim and the liquid, never the image. Paper and tape keep their own colours in both lights.

rules.name: The Legible Room Rule
rules.body: Every text pair holds at least 4.5:1 in both lights. Measured in the build: muted on room 7.3:1 (4.98:1 at the pool's centre), tape-ink-2 on tape 6.2:1, lights-on muted on room 5.7:1, sign text on the red plate 4.5:1 at its lightest stop, lights-on sign text 4.5:1, loupe labels 5.2:1.

rules.name: The Grease Pencil Rule
rules.body: Permanent Marker is only for what a hand would write on tape: the print number, its title, the subtitle. Everything printed, signed or measured is Barlow Condensed.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: The only radial gradient in the room is the safelight pool on the room itself. Trays, prints, tape, sign and tubs never carry a radial glow; their light comes from linear sheens and the rim's lit edge.

dos: Do size every print from its own width-to-height ratio, in the tray, on the line, on the wall and in the loupe.
Do keep the photograph's colours untouched once developed; the safelight colours the room, not the image.
Do caption a print with "No. n" and only the title, place, year and camera details that exist.
Do take every colour from the safelight and lights-on tokens, and hold every text pair at 4.5:1 or more in both lights.
Do keep the ripple overscanned inside a clipped frame so the photo edge stays square.
Do give every new motion an instant, settled state under reduced motion.
donts: Don't put a tint, overlay or colour filter over a developed photograph.
Don't crop or force a photograph into a fixed aspect ratio.
Don't show file names anywhere: not in captions, alt text or labels.
Don't cut torn or deckled edges with clip-path; paper and tape are straight-cut.
Don't draw stripes or textures with repeating gradients.
Don't put a radial glow on a surface; the safelight pool on the room is the only radial light.
Don't use hard offset shadows; shadows are soft and fall from real objects.
Don't bring homepage devices (spines, ticks, STIX, DejaVu, tab blue) into the darkroom.
